newsitem.title: USA: United agrees to wage increase for machinists.
newsitem.headline: United agrees to wage increase for machinists.

text.p: UAL Corp's United Airlines said Friday it reached a tentative agreement with the International Association of Machinists (IAM), which is one of the union groups that holds a stake in the airline.
UAL said the pact increases wages by three percent in both 1997 and 1998, and by two percent in both 1999 and 2000, United said.

Also, the 24,000 machininsts are eligible for lump-sum profit-sharing payments of up to two percent in 1998 and 1999, depending on the company's performance in 1997 and 1998, respectively, the airline said.
The pact represents a mid-term wage adjustment, a process designed to ensure the wages keep pace with the rest of the industry, United said.
"This (wage adjustment) is just to make sure the gap doesn't widen further between us and the industry," UAL spokesman Tony Molinaro said.
IAM-represented employees will vote on the tentative agreement during the week of January 6, United said.
In late November, it reached a similar wage increase agreement with the Air Line Pilots Association, covering 8,500 United pilots.
The wage adjustment was built into UAL's July 1994 ESOP, when the pilots, machinists and salaried employees swapped wage cuts and work rule changes for a majority stake in the airline.
Donaldson, Lufkin and Jenrette analyst James Higgins said the wage increase for the machinsts was a little higher than he expected.
"I would have liked to see a little less," Higgins added. "It does place some pressure on their (UAL's) costs."
Molinaro said discussions are under way about a possible wage increase for its 33,000 management and non-union employees, following agreements reached with two of its unions.
UAL shares were down three at 60 in late afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange, after closing Thursday near its 52-week high.
